retro:
# Retrospective: PR #12884 follow-up

## Worked

Fresh independent sessions received only the public historical claim, author reply, pinned revisions and neutral scope. Opus ran through Claude Code's existing authentication route at xhigh; Astra remained xhigh. Equivalent scope did not force duplicate methods: Astra exercised modeled arrival/signal wiring and both representative choices, while Opus isolated the fix with a one-line mutation and positive/negative regression controls. Both distinguished per-delegate countdown behavior from timestamps. No generic tests or extra findings were manufactured.

## Friction and correction

Astra's first isolated setup lacked Node on the sanitized PATH. It stopped before behavior tests, preserved the failed sealed bundle and used the documented hash-pinned executable-copy method in a new fixture version. This is a setup limitation, not a PR defect or an unsandboxed fallback. Opus independently used the same supported packaging method.

A coordinator lifecycle screen read requested scrollback while Claude's effort selector was blocked. Herdr rejected the read. The coordinator used visible-screen inspection instead; no context, session or safety boundary changed. Record as tool-interface friction rather than reviewer contamination.

**Process deviation PR12884-PD1:** Opus's runner records syntax/probe exits but does not immediately assert every non-Node probe or syntax result. This violates the mandatory fail-fast rule even though all actual prerequisites returned zero. The coordinator initially misclassified it as a robustness observation and incorrectly marked process compliance true. That attestation is now false. Evidence remains in `reviewers/opus/fixture/runner.py` and the sealed run's `output/results.json`; prior coordinator metadata is preserved under `metadata-history/pre-fail-fast-correction/`.

No technical impact was identified: every prerequisite's successful child status and raw output was inspected, no failed prerequisite underlies accepted claims, and independent Astra evidence remains valid. This process-only deviation does not block publication once the outer freshness checks pass. Technical synthesis, exact public draft, draft hash and existing editorial pass remain unchanged. No new technical work or editorial check was performed.

Concrete assignment correction: require an immediate status/timeout assertion after every syntax, extraction, import, version, capability and readiness prerequisite, before running any dependent case. Post-run inspection does not substitute for fail-fast enforcement. Preserve failed outputs and stop dependent work if any prerequisite fails.

Final discussion refetch detected an edited author reply. Exact comparison showed only an added `@llstrk` mention and removal of a trailing newline, with no changed technical claim or question. The final edited snapshot is recorded. An initial exact-equality assertion correctly stopped snapshot preparation; a subsequent editorial-launch command then failed because requirements had not yet been written. No editorial process started in that failed attempt. Preparation was corrected and a new check launched from complete immutable inputs. This did not invalidate technical evidence.

## Limits and cleanup

No native QML or desktop timing validation occurred. The public draft explicitly limits the current evidence to modeled service behavior and source-derived countdown semantics. Old native measurements are historical only. No desktop slots or host services were used. Private runner children completed and were reaped; no persistent resource required termination. Source trees, failed and valid sealed bundles, session histories and reviewer panes are preserved. The fail-fast process deviation above is explicitly recorded; no resulting evidence-integrity, safety-boundary or reviewer-independence impact was identified. No Omadev defect is claimed.

## Carry forward

Read the countdown owner, not just a plausible timestamp field. Retain useful negative controls and positive control of extracted tests. Plan private interpreter availability before fixture pinning, without host runtime probes. Publicly confirm a resolved finding when evidence supports it; keep unrelated pre-existing questions local. The coordinator never opens the saved reader or posts upstream.
comment:
**Verified: the [earlier update-lifetime finding](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12884#issuecomment-5775973256) is resolved at `f7df713b`.** A content-changing group member now takes the singleton insertion path rather than arrival deduplication. No new issue was found in this follow-up's directly affected scope.

Production service functions exercised with synthetic notifications and a modeled ListModel gave this result, including when the changed member was the original group representative:

| Changed A member becomes B while an older B popup exists | Original `81d2031d` | Current `f7df713b` |
|---|---|---|
| Updated member | Joins the older B row | Gets a separate singleton row |
| Explicitly expire the older B popup | Updated member closes too | Updated member remains tracked |

The separate row gets its own countdown according to the inspected delegate code; elapsed native-QML timing was not rerun. Ordinary new-arrival grouping remains intact.

**Verified:** All three notification test scripts pass at the current head. The added regression case passes there and fails at the separate-membership assertion against both the original revision and a diagnostic one-line revert of the fix.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Scoped original/current source comparison, independent modeled service tests and repository notification tests. Notification objects, ListModel and persistence were modeled; full desktop rendering, native D-Bus/QML timing, real application integration and restart persistence were not retested end to end.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Fresh independent Opus 5 xhigh and Astra Xhigh follow-up assessments, followed by Astra coordination, synthesis and verification against source and saved targeted evidence.
